title: ALL CAPS: THE HISTORY OF THE AMERICAN BASEBALL HAT
chaptersLine: Forty-plus chapters drafted, plus an introduction and a closing coda.
spanLine: From before the Civil War to the drops of 2026.
thisWeek: The master manuscript got touched again midweek, another pass with the voice rules on.
Two long-open factual questions were run down and closed, one about language and one about a nineteenth century catalog.
Two research intakes landed this week, both keyed to chapters already drafted.
chapterHighlights: A hat shop that has held the same block of East Los Angeles for twenty years, and what that block has always meant.
How a cap first became something you could order by model number, out of a book, sight unseen.
The pillbox, the cartoon bird, the winged A: caps whose own teams eventually thought better of them.
The Negro Leagues chapter, told through the caps that survived and the ones that did not.
